```{r, include = FALSE}
  collapse = TRUE,

  eval = TRUE

```

`ocean3d` is built on terra: `SpatVoxel` and `SpatEnvelope` are terra
`SpatRaster`s, so terra functions still work on them. terra can record the
depth of each layer with `terra::depth()`, but its functions treat the layers
as a stack. They don't use the depth to decide which cells a shape covers, and
a raster has no way to store a depth range per cell. This article shows the
difference on a small example.

## The example

A species lives between the surface and 150 m, or the seafloor where it is
shallower, in three of four cells. Temperature is known at 0, 100 and 200 m.

```{r setup}
library(terra)
library(ocean3d)

# Temperature at 0, 100 and 200 m on a 2 x 2 grid
temp <- rast(nrows = 2, ncols = 2, nlyrs = 3,
             xmin = 0, xmax = 2, ymin = 0, ymax = 2)
values(temp) <- rep(c(20, 15, 8), each = 4)
depth(temp) <- c(0, 100, 200)

seafloor <- setValues(rast(temp, nlyrs = 1), c(50, 150, 250, 250))
range_2d <- setValues(rast(temp, nlyrs = 1), c(1, 1, 1, NA))
```

## With terra

`terra::mask()` applies the 2D range to every layer, whatever its depth. The
first cell keeps its temperatures at 100 m and 200 m, although the seafloor
there is at 50 m. Leaving out the layers below 150 m, or below the seafloor in
each cell, has to be done by hand.

```{r terra-mask}
values(mask(temp, range_2d))
```

## With ocean3d

The range becomes a 3D envelope, with `depth_min` and `depth_max` in each
cell. `mask()` then keeps only the depth levels inside the envelope in each
cell, and `volume()` gives the volume of the envelope.

```{r ocean3d-mask}
voxel <- as_voxel(temp, depths = c(0, 100, 200), varname = "temp")
habitat <- as_envelope(range_2d, depth_min = 0,
                       depth_max = min(seafloor, 150))
values(mask(voxel, habitat))

volume(habitat) # km³
```

How an envelope's depth range is matched to the depth levels is set out in
`vignette("depth-levels")`.

## Depth in layer names

`ocean3d` stores depth in layer names (`{variable}_depth={value}`) for now.
The planned data model
([#99](https://github.com/Marine-Biodiversity-Conservation-Lab/ocean3d/issues/99))
moves it to `terra::depth()`, so voxels will use terra's own depth field.
